summary: Build a neural system that answers typed questions with probability distributions, then separate its learned beliefs from calibrated evidence and cost-sensitive actions. Connect an inspectable encoder decision head to an end-to-end research project without assuming that Jev and Laya share undisclosed internals.
outcomes: Distinguish fixed-label classification, schema-conditioned candidate scoring and constrained autoregressive generation, including what each output contract guarantees
Trace state, instructions, candidate descriptions, marker positions, padding and question types through a bidirectional encoder and a shared option scorer
Implement and inspect a small decision head, masked stable softmax, ordinal expectation and binary truth probability before using a pretrained library model
Derive the probability-reporting objective, compare direct supervised optimization with a policy-gradient estimator, and test scoring-rule orientation and ordinal category order
Fit calibration on a separate partition, evaluate on untouched test data, and distinguish entropy concentration, accuracy, calibration and operational risk
Choose actions and abstention from a stated loss table and a measured fallback rather than from an arbitrary confidence threshold
Investigate candidate permutation, distractors, wording, missing choices, context truncation, language shift and changing candidate counts
Produce a reproducible checkpoint and research report with complete preprocessing, candidate schemas, split identities, environment and evidence limits
sequence: Begin with a concrete document-routing decision: distinguish available evidence, candidate meaning, a probability report and the downstream action
Compare three output mechanisms on the same task: a fixed classifier, a dynamic option-marker head and grammar-constrained generation; identify schema validity versus semantic correctness
Inspect a compact input sequence, attention mask, candidate positions and shared scoring path; connect ModernBERT/mmBERT to the encoder-foundations owner without duplicating its full implementation
Build the decision head and typed outputs from scratch, including candidate masking, stable probability normalization, gradients and replayable toy fixtures
Train a direct soft-target baseline; extend prior log/Brier scoring to spherical and ranked probability scores, then derive and compare a probability-policy estimator with group baselines
Use explicit train, model-selection validation, calibration and test partitions; freeze selection, calibrate probabilities and report uncertainty and subgroup limits
Convert calibrated probabilities into cost-sensitive actions and abstention; investigate why a concentrated distribution can still be systematically wrong
Bridge the scratch components to current library APIs and pinned checkpoints; examine batching, routing, cold starts, memory, language support and serialization
Run controlled ablations and shift tests, distinguish published implementation evidence from vendor claims, and continue into the linked end-to-end decision-model project

visual.question: Which change affects the representation, the probability report, its measured reliability or the action, and what evidence lets us tell those effects apart?
visual.interaction: Show current outputs immediately. Change candidate descriptions or toy representations, temperature and action costs with appropriate live controls; compare preserved runs. Use explicit bounded training steps for expensive processes, label simulated versus checkpoint-backed results, provide keyboard equivalents, and never ask for a learner prediction to reveal an answer.

practice.task: Implement and verify the option scorer, compare direct and policy-gradient training on a controlled dataset, fit a separate calibration partition, add a new candidate schema, and investigate one failure under a changed cost matrix or shifted language/input distribution.
practice.success: Shows independently checked probabilities and gradients, preserves candidate identity and ordinal meaning, prevents split leakage, measures uncertainty and actual decision costs, and states which conclusions come from toy calculations, local experiments or external reports.
